pr.title: Forbid ShallowInitBox after box deref elaboration.
pr.description:
MIR currently contains a `ShallowInitBox` rvalue. Its principal usage is to allow for in-place initialization of boxes. Having it is necessary for drop elaboration to be correct with that in-place initialization.

As part of analysis->runtime MIR lowering, we canonicalize deref of boxes to use the stored raw pointer. But we did not perform the same change to the construction of the box.

This PR replaces `ShallowInitBox` by the pointer manipulation it represents.

Alternatives:
- fully remove `ShallowInitBox` and implement `Box` in-place initialization differently;
- remove the `ElaborateBoxDeref` pass and keep dereferencing `Box` in runtime MIR.

pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The historical change (PR #147687) is a MIR canonicalization/phase-invariant change, not a semantic miscompile. The old `ShallowInitBox(ptr, T)` codegen path already treated the raw allocation pointer as the `Box<T>` value; the new expansion reconstructs the same `Box<T>` value from the same pointer via `*const T -> NonNull<T> -> Unique<T> -> Box<T>`, with the `PhantomData` marker and `Global` allocator fields being zero-sized. No source-level Rust program can distinguish the two representations on concrete inputs, and the PR/analysis explicitly warn not to invent a runtime-value difference. The visible MIR diffs (`Transmute` -> `PtrToPtr`, `move` -> `copy`, local renumbering) are GVN/representation effects on the reshaped MIR, not semantic changes. Thus no legitimate source-grounded original/transformed pair can exhibit differing Miri results.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `ElaborateBoxDerefs` only rewrote place projections through `Box`: `Box` is not actually a pointer, so dereferencing it directly is incorrect at runtime. The pass's old comment states: "This pass transforms derefs of Box into a deref of the pointer inside Box." However, it did not rewrite the *construction* of a box. Analysis-phase MIR uses `Rvalue::ShallowInitBox(mutptr, pointee)` for in-place box initialization, and that rvalue survived into runtime MIR. The PR description explains: "As part of analysis->runtime MIR lowering, we canonicalize deref of boxes to use the stored raw pointer. But we did not perform the same change to the construction of the box."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically incorrect transformation: after running `ElaborateBoxDerefs`, an assignment such as `_7 = ShallowInitBox(move _6, i32)` was left in runtime MIR while box derefs were already canonicalized to the stored pointer. Thus construction and dereference used inconsistent representations. The fix replaces that rvalue with the pointer manipulation it represents: transmute the initializing `*mut u8` to the pointee pointer, build `NonNull`, build `Unique` (with its `PhantomData` marker), then build `Box` (with the allocator/`Global` field as a zero-sized constant). The PR body states: "This PR replaces `ShallowInitBox` by the pointer manipulation it represents." This is a phase-invariant/canonicalization change, not evidence that the old MIR produced different runtime values; do not invent a semantic miscompile.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR at analysis -> runtime lowering, specifically around `MirPhase::Runtime(RuntimePhase::Initial)`, for bodies that allocate/initialize a `Box` (e.g. `Box::new`, `box expr`, inlined `exchange_malloc`) and also dereference box values. Pointee types observed in tests include `i32`, `()`, and user structs (`S`); both `panic-abort` and `panic-unwind` MIR are in scope. `ShallowInitBox` may legitimately exist before elaboration in analysis MIR, but must not remain in runtime MIR.
analysis.summary: `ElaborateBoxDerefs` canonicalizes `Box` derefs to the stored raw pointer. This PR also makes it canonicalize box *construction*: every `Rvalue::ShallowInitBox(raw_ptr, T)` in runtime MIR is expanded into `Cast(Transmute)` to `*const T`, then `NonNull<T>`, then `Unique<T>` with `PhantomData`, then `Box<T>` with `Global`. Afterwards `ShallowInitBox` is forbidden in runtime MIR: `Validator` rejects it after `RuntimePhase::Initial`, and `GVN`/`DataflowConstProp` treat it as a bug rather than an unsupported value. Reusable invariant: if a pass changes how `Box` values are represented for dereference, it must change construction of those values in the same phase.
analysis.trigger: Run `ElaborateBoxDerefs` over MIR containing `_b = ShallowInitBox(mutptr, T)` (box allocation/in-place initialization) and/or `ProjectionElem::Deref` on a `Box<T>`; the fixed pass must eliminate every `ShallowInitBox` and produce an explicit `Box` aggregate chain.
preconditions: The body has reached runtime-phase lowering where `Box` derefs have been elaborated; the new `Validator` check fires at `self.body.phase >= MirPhase::Runtime(RuntimePhase::Initial)`.

`Box`, `Unique`, `NonNull`, and the allocator (`Global`) lang/ADT types are resolvable, with `Box` field 0 = `Unique`, `Box` field 1 = allocator, `Unique` field 0 = `NonNull`, `Unique` field 1 = `PhantomData`.
The `ShallowInitBox` operand is the raw allocation pointer; the second argument is the pointee type used to instantiate `*const T`, `NonNull<T>`, `Unique<T>`, and `Box<T>`.
Analysis-phase MIR may still contain `ShallowInitBox`; only runtime MIR is required to be free of it.
pitfalls: Elaborating only derefs but not `ShallowInitBox` leaves mixed `Box` representation; downstream passes either silently bail (`GVN` previously returned `None`, `DataflowConstProp` treated it as TOP) or, after this PR, panic because it is forbidden in runtime MIR.

Build ADT types from the resolved `ty::AdtDef` with the right generic args (`Ty::new_adt`, `tcx.mk_args(&[pointee.into()])`), not from a bare `DefId`; the patch also changes `build_ptr_tys` to accept `ty::AdtDef<'tcx>`.

The `Box` allocator field and the `Unique` marker field are not both `PhantomData`: use the actual field types (`unique_def.non_enum_variant().fields[FieldIdx::ONE]` and `box_adt.non_enum_variant().fields[FieldIdx::ONE]`) as zero-sized constants.
The `Validator` deref-of-`Box` phase gate moved from `RuntimePhase::PostCleanup` to `RuntimePhase::Initial`; checking too late can miss residual box derefs.

Do not conflate the box-construction rewrite with downstream GVN effects visible in the same diffs (e.g. `Transmute` becoming `PtrToPtr`, or `move` becoming `copy`); those are GVN results on the newly shaped MIR, not part of `ElaborateBoxDerefs`.
Borrowing/post-copy overwrite details in the decoded diffs are separate conditions; do not use them to claim a different box-construction bug.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/mir-opt` with `// EMIT_MIR` and CHECK lines. For a program that allocates and initializes a box (`Box::new`/`box expr`, including non-ZST `i32`, ZST `()`, and a user struct `S`), run `ElaborateBoxDerefs` and assert the output has no `ShallowInitBox`. Assert the exact replacement chain, e.g. the added test expects `[[ptr]] = move _ as *const S (Transmute); [[nonnull]] = NonNull::<S> { pointer: move [[ptr]] }; [[unique]] = Unique::<S> { pointer: move [[nonnull]], _marker: const PhantomData::<S> }; [[box]] = Box::<S>(move [[unique]], const std::alloc::Global);`. Compare panic-abort and panic-unwind outputs (`const_prop/boxes.main.GVN.*.diff`) where the old MIR showed `_7 = ShallowInitBox(move _6, i32);` and the corrected revision shows `_7 = Box::<i32>(move _10, const std::alloc::Global);`. Add negative/validator coverage for any hand-written runtime MIR retaining `ShallowInitBox` (expected diagnostic: `ShallowInitBox after ElaborateBoxDerefs`). No compiler was built here; never claim execution or reproduction.
